alt: French Mandate of Syria and Lebanon
Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon
wikipedia: Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon

predecessors.name: Arab Kingdom of Syria
predecessors.text: Faisal's Arab Kingdom of Syria, whose capital Damascus Gouraud's forces 'captured ... with little resistance' on 24 July 1920

predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: the coast and mountain of Lebanon, proclaimed the State of Greater Lebanon on 1 September 1920, and the Syrian coast

successors.name: Second Syrian Republic
successors.text: Syria: 'Syria became fully independent on 17 April 1946' and 'The French evacuated the last of their troops in April of that year' (Levant Crisis page)

successors.name: Lebanon
successors.text: 'Lebanon became an independent state on 22 November 1943' (Syria-Lebanon campaign page)

successors.name: Hatay State
successors.text: the Sanjak of Alexandretta, proclaimed the Hatay State on 2 September 1938 and annexed by Turkey by 23 July 1939

ledger.x: April 1920: the mandate holds the French-occupied Cilician belt.
1920: the Allies give France the mandate for Syria and Lebanon.
24 July 1920: the French win at Maysaloun 'in less than a day' and Gouraud's forces capture Damascus; the page records no further fighting of the war.
January 1922: France leaves the Cilician belt.
January 1922: the strip north of the Ankara line passes to Turkey.
7 March 1923: the Franco-British frontier is settled.
21 July 1925: the Druze win the battle of al-Kafr, the first fight of the Great Syrian Revolt that holds ground.
2 September 1938: the Sanjak of Alexandretta becomes the Hatay State.
8 June 1941: British, Commonwealth and Free French forces invade the Vichy-held mandate.
14 July 1941: Vichy forces yield by the Armistice of Saint Jean d'Acre.
July 1941: the mandate passes from Vichy France to Free France.

wars.name: Franco-Syrian War
wars.outcome: French victory at Maysaloun in less than a day; Damascus taken on 24 July 1920 and the Arab Kingdom of Syria ended.

wars.name: Franco-Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Ankara Agreement of 20 October 1921 ended the war and France ceded Adana, Osmaniye, Marash, Aintab, Kilis, Urfa, Mardin, Nusaybin and Cizre to Turkey; the French forces withdrew from the occupation zone in the first days of 1922 (completed 7 January).

wars.name: Great Syrian Revolt
wars.outcome: French victory: the uprisings 'continued until late June 1927'; Sultan al-Atrash went into exile in Transjordan and Shahbandar fled to Transjordan and then Egypt.

wars.name: Syria-Lebanon campaign
wars.outcome: Allied victory: ceasefire 12 July and the Armistice of Saint Jean d'Acre on 14 July 1941; Free France took over the administration of both territories.

wars.name: Levant Crisis
wars.outcome: British-Syrian victory; the British ordered the French to cease fire on 31 May 1945 and the French withdrew, the last troops leaving in April 1946.

certainty.note: Military occupation lines: the Cilician belt and the strip along the Turkish side were French-held (since the landing at Mersin on 17 November 1918) until the evacuation of the first days of January 1922 that followed the Ankara Agreement…
The Turkish frontier follows the 1921 agreement (the Baghdad Railway to Nusaybin); the Hatay cut of 1938-39 is dated.
